thread:
Priya: Quick intake — I'd like to propose onboarding mistral-13b-v1 (fp16) plus a q4_0 quantized variant into the model catalog for Hosted + Dedicated. Observed ~8-12% higher pass@k on our codegen evals vs current 13B. Want to capture perf, cost, and regression risk before we flip it on for prod.

Marcus: Can you drop the initial benchmark results and the bring-up checklist here? Also call out any safety / opt-out considerations.

Priya: TL;DR benchmarks:
- eval/codegen-suite: rouge/acc improvements across 3 workloads: +9%, +8%, +12%
- latency (p99 tokens/sec, 2048 context, batch=1): fp16 = 82 ms/token, q4_0 = 68 ms/token
- cost estimate (token units): q4_0 roughly 0.55x current 13B fp16 per-token GPU time

Marcus: Nice. How stable are the q4 outputs? Any hallucination spike?

Priya: Ran the qual/regression harness: small uptick in long-document factuality failures on the summarization suite (~1.4% -> 1.8%). Codegen and dialog tasks unchanged. We flagged 12 prompts as regressions and added them to the regression set.

Ava: Proposed bring-up checklist (short):
1) Model card draft + license check
2) Safety evals: toxicity, jailbreaks, privacy probes
3) Quantization sweep: q4_0, q4_1, q8_0 if feasible
4) Perf bench: latency/cold start/throughput across our instance types
5) Cost model update (token-unit delta + suggested route)
6) Catalog entry + metadata (families, tags, compatible fallbacks)
7) Rollout plan: canary percentage, fallback policy, canary duration
8) Docs + release note + marketing sync
9) Monitoring hooks: qualitative evals, drift alerts, token-level cost reports

Sam: From product/marketing side: we need the model-card + a 1-paragraph "what's better" and any breaking behavior for users. Also add a changelog line for the Console and an admin toggle in Dedicated.

Priya: Pasted commands we used to run the perf/quant bench: 
```
# example: run local quant bench
python tools/bench.py --model mistral-13b-v1 --quant q4_0 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --shots 0
# perf summary saved to /tmp/mistral_q4_bench.json
```

Marcus: Can you also add the exact eval harness command (so QA can reproduce)?

Priya: Yup, added: 
```
python eval/harness.py --suite codegen --model mistral-13b-v1 --quant q4_0 --seed 42 --out results/mistral_codegen_q4.json
```

MarketingBot: @Sam reminder: we have the broadcast cadence doc at https://wiki.redwood/team/marketing/release-cadence — want to slot this in for next-week product digest if approved.

Ava: Risks to call out in catalog entry: quantized variant deterministic differences (non-bit-identical), slight summarization regressions on >10k tokens, no new safety categories triggered in our static suite.

Priya: Action items:
- Priya: finish model card + safety eval summary by EOD Thu (1718284800) :white_check_mark:
- Marcus: run q4_1 sweep and sanity tests on Dedicated nodes by Fri :eyes:
- Ava: create draft catalog entry + metadata + rollback policy by Mon
- Sam: prepare marketing blurb and console changelog entries, coordinate final publish window

CI-Bot: Artifact built: model package mistral-13b-v1@sha256:abcd1234. Perf artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-model-bench/mistral/171820/

Marcus: I'll start the q4_1 sweep now and post a short summary. Expect 1-2 hours.

Priya: Thanks — once we have q4_1 numbers and Marcus' sanity checks, I'll open the catalog PR and a docs PR with the release notes. Planning a 10% canary for Hosted with automatic fallback to current-13b if latency or error-rate exceeds thresholds.

Sam: Sounds good. @MarketingBot let's tentatively aim the external mention for Wed after internal validation.

Ava: Noted. I'll include monitoring dashboards (tokens, p99 latency, regressions) in the catalog entry.

Marcus: Quick note — if q4_1 matches q4_0 perf but reduces regressions, prefer q4_1 for Dedicated initial rollout.

Priya: Agreed. Will compare after sweep and pick the quant that balances cost + quality.

Marcus: posted q4_1 quick results: latency ~72 ms/token, regressions reduced to 1.5%. Attaching summary file: s3://redwood-model-bench/mistral/q4_sweep_summary.json

Priya: Great — moving forward to PRs. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
